scope: Actual paired boundary coefficient cancellation, mass/log cutoff regularity, and quantitative diagnosis of an excessive gluing certificate. No determinant-limit theorem or full signed projection.
ordinary_argument_review: The actual first-order pair has complementary adjoint domains. Keep the induced square boundary condition, physical-half normalization, thermal bolt and identical scalar deformations.
At the limiting seam the physical phase preserves K=S=0 and chi_:a=0. Rank-two E is scalar and normal-tangential spin curvature anticommutes with chi.
The inward a4 boundary derivative cancels the integrated bulk divergence. All remaining a5 mixed traces cancel algebraically, before a potentially undefined fourth log jet is evaluated.
The smooth coefficient theorem supplies a counterterm test only. Its hypotheses do not give a heat expansion on the actual log phase; a5 cancellation is not a regulator theorem.
The mass cubic has an H3 approximation but its fourth derivative cost grows as inverse cutoff. This tests a proof strategy, not a substituted smooth geometry or a physical obstruction.

The prior candidate weak-form closure retains its scope. Identifying it with two derivatives of the commonly regulated functional requires a uniform approximation/regulator bound, not just boundedness of a limiting form.
A Dini heat majorant would justify the ultraviolet step; its constant is unknown. Evaluate sufficient power and log thresholds at actual physical constants.
The existing gluing allowance is a known upper certificate. Its large size is not an actual source value or a nonexistence result.
Park the adiabatic coefficient extension and numerical projection until the actual-domain uniform identification is established. Do not optimize the controlled cold or scalar components.
